question: Does the professional translation or the machine translation introduce the artifacts?

evidence: In this paper, we have shown that both human and machine translation can alter superficial patterns in data, which requires reconsidering previous findings in cross-lingual transfer learning. Based on the gained insights, we have improved the state-of-the-art in XNLI for the Translate-Test and Zero-Shot approaches by a substantial margin. Finally, we have shown that the phenomenon is not specific to NLI but also affects QA, although it is less pronounced there thanks to the translation procedure used in the corresponding benchmarks. So as to facilitate similar studies in the future, we release our NLI dataset, which, unlike previous benchmarks, was annotated in a non-English language and human translated into English.

title: Translation Artifacts in Cross-lingual Transfer Learning
answer_rationale: The documents indicate that both professional and machine translation can introduce artifacts. Text 1 states that translation processes, whether human or machine, can introduce subtle artifacts. Text 3 further clarifies that these artifacts arise from the translation process itself, particularly when translating different parts of an instance separately, which affects model performance. Text 5 also notes that translation artifacts are present in both human and machine translation contexts, especially when combined in Translate-Test scenarios.
